# Malaria RCT Brief

Automated weekly scan for new malaria randomized controlled trials.
Sources: PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, Europe PMC (incl. medRxiv preprints and
Cochrane review metadata). Most recent week on top. The structured dataset lives
in data/trials.csv.

## Week of 2026-09-21

### Protective efficacy and user acceptability of DEET and Vetiver essential oil repellents against Anopheles dirus (Diptera: Culicidae): semi-field and community-based evaluations.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (42762484)
- **Journal:** Journal of medical entomology
- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Not applicable
- **Place:** Thailand, Khun Han District, Sisaket Province
- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2026-09-01
- **Class:** spatial repellent
- **Population:** community residents
- **N:** 457
- **Impact:** DEET substantially reduced mosquito landing (95.75%) in semi-field trials while Vetiver essential oil showed only moderate protection (51.9%), and in the community trial Vetiver E.O.'s reported efficacy and acceptability were comparable to placebo, indicating insufficient real-world biological activity.
- **Effect:** percentage reduction in mosquito landing DEET 95.75%, Vetiver E.O. 51.9%
- **Follow-up:** 9 months
- **Link:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42762484/

### Impact of mass distribution on insecticide-treated net coverage and usage in three high burden malaria provinces of Papua New Guinea.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (42736560)
- **Journal:** Infectious diseases of poverty
- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Not applicable
- **Place:** Papua New Guinea
- **Design:** cross-sectional surveys, before-after, generalised linear mixed effects models
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2026-09-14
- **Trial period:** 2023 to 2024
- **Class:** ITN/LLIN
- **Population:** individuals and households in East Sepik, West Sepik and Madang provinces
- **N:** 5671
- **Impact:** Mass ITN distribution increased household net ownership from 94.8% to 99.4% and universal coverage from 60.0% to 69.9%, with usage driven primarily by net availability.
- **Effect:** change in universal coverage (%) 60.0% to 69.9%
- **Follow-up:** 5-7 months post-distribution
- **Link:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42736560/

### Baseline Treg frequency, Treg-associated immune checkpoint responses, and plasma IL-10 responses during controlled human malaria infection in semi-immune Kenyan adults: a secondary analysis of the CHMI-SIKA Study.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (42398508)
- **Journal:** The Lancet. Microbe
- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Not applicable
- **Place:** Kenya
- **Design:** controlled human malaria infection, secondary analysis
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2026-07-03
- **Class:** vaccine
- **Population:** semi-immune Kenyan adults from three regions with differing P falciparum exposure
- **N:** 105
- **Impact:** High baseline Treg frequencies were associated with upregulation of TNFRSF18, LRRC32, and KLRG1 in Tregs, increased P falciparum parasite growth, and higher IL-10 concentrations in treated compared with untreated semi-immune Kenyan adults.
- **Effect:** Number of differentially expressed genes between treated and untreated participants 15 differentially expressed genes at day 8
- **Species:** P. falciparum
- **Follow-up:** 35 days
- **Link:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42398508/

## Week of 2026-08-10

### Comparing Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine+Chloroquine and Dihydroartemisinin-Piperaquine to Control for Malaria Prevention in Malawian School Children: Results from a Randomized Controlled Trial
- **Source / ID:** europepmc (PPR1294155)
- **Journal:** medRxiv
- **Type:** preprint
- **Phase:** Phase 3
- **Place:** Malawi
- **Design:** 3-arm randomized controlled trial, modified intention-to-treat
- **Status:** preprint
- **Published:** 2026-08-07
- **Class:** IPTsc; treatment/ACT
- **Population:** Primary school children
- **N:** 646
- **Impact:** Both IPTsc with Dihydroartemisinin-Piperaquine and Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine+Chloroquine significantly reduced malaria infection, anemia, and clinical malaria compared to control, with SP+CQ shown to be a suitable alternative to DP.
- **Effect:** adjusted Odds Ratio (infection) DP: aOR 0.22; SP+CQ: aOR 0.38 (95% CI DP: 0.14-0.36; SP+CQ: 0.24-0.59)
- **Species:** P. falciparum
- **Follow-up:** 6-8 weeks after final dose
- **Link:** https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.04.26359752

## Week of 2026-08-07

### Evaluating controlled human malaria infection in Kenyan adults with varying degrees of prior exposure to Plasmodium falciparum using sporozoites administered by intramuscular injection.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (25566206)
- **Journal:** Frontiers in microbiology
- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Phase II
- **Place:** Kenya
- **Design:** open-label, randomized, pilot study, phase II
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2014-12-12
- **Class:** vaccine
- **Population:** Kenyan adults with low to moderate prior exposure to P. falciparum
- **N:** 28
- **Impact:** PfSPZ Challenge was safe and infectious in Kenyan adults, and one volunteer with high prior exposure showed a markedly reduced parasite multiplication rate, suggesting naturally-acquired immunity can impact parasite growth dynamics post-CHMI.
- **Effect:** correlation between parasite multiplication rate and screening anti-schizont ELISA OD R = -0.384
- **Species:** P. falciparum
- **Follow-up:** 21 days
- **Link:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25566206/

### Artemisinin-naphthoquine versus artemether-lumefantrine for uncomplicated malaria in Papua New Guinean children: an open-label randomized trial.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (25549086)
- **Journal:** PLoS medicine
- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Phase 3
- **Place:** Papua New Guinea
- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2014-12-30
- **Trial period:** 2011 to 2013
- **Class:** treatment/ACT
- **Population:** children aged 0.5-5 years with uncomplicated malaria
- **N:** 267
- **Impact:** Artemisinin-naphthoquine was non-inferior to artemether-lumefantrine for falciparum malaria but showed substantially greater efficacy against vivax malaria.
- **Effect:** difference in ACPR (%) P. falciparum: 2.2% difference; P. vivax: 70.0% difference (95% CI P. falciparum: -3.0% to 8.4%; P. vivax: 40.9%-87.2%)
- **Species:** mixed
- **Follow-up:** 42 days
- **Link:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25549086/

### Fixed dose artesunate amodiaquine - a phase IIb, randomized comparative trial with non-fixed artesunate amodiaquine.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (25515698)
- **Journal:** Malaria journal
- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Phase IIb
- **Place:** Kenya
- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2014-12-16
- **Trial period:** 2007 to 2008
- **Class:** treatment/ACT
- **Population:** adults with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
- **N:** 54
- **Impact:** Fixed dose and non-fixed dose artesunate amodiaquine showed similar pharmacokinetic exposure for dihydroartemisinin equivalents and comparable, rapid parasite clearance rates, with good tolerability for both formulations.
- **Effect:** Mean AUC0-72 of DHA equivalents 24.2 vs 26.4 µmol*h/L
- **Species:** P. falciparum
- **Follow-up:** 28 days
- **Link:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25515698/

### Economic evaluation of a cluster randomized trial of interventions to improve health workers' practice in diagnosing and treating uncomplicated malaria in Cameroon.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (25498773)
- **Journal:** Value in health : the journal of the International Society for Pharmacoeconomics and Outcomes Research
- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Not applicable
- **Place:** Cameroon
- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2014-10-07
- **Class:** treatment/ACT; diagnostic
- **Population:** febrile patients attending health facilities; health workers in health facilities
- **N:** 46
- **Impact:** Introducing RDTs with enhanced training was more cost-effective than RDTs with basic training when each was compared with current practice.
- **Effect:** incremental cost per febrile patient correctly treated $8.40 (basic arm), $3.71 (enhanced arm); enhanced training saves $0.75 per additional febrile patient correctly treated on scale-up
- **Species:** P. falciparum
- **Link:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25498773/

### Strengthening malaria service delivery through supportive supervision and community mobilization in an endemic Indian setting: an evaluation of nested delivery models.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (25491041)
- **Journal:** Malaria journal
- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Not applicable
- **Place:** India (Odisha)
- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2014-12-08
- **Class:** ITN/LLIN
- **Population:** villagers in malaria-endemic districts, including fever cases and women
- **N:** 120
- **Impact:** Community-based interventions combining supportive supervision of community health workers with community mobilization improved bed net use and timely care-seeking for fever from trained providers compared to control villages.
- **Effect:** percentage point difference in outcome proportions bed net use 84.5% (arm A) and 82.4% (arm B) vs 78.6% (control); timely treatment from skilled provider within 24 hours 60.6% (combined arm) and 59.3% (community mobilization arm) vs 50.1% (control)
- **Link:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25491041/

### The outcome of a test-treat package versus routine outpatient care for Ghanaian children with fever: a pragmatic randomized control trial.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (25428264)
- **Journal:** Malaria journal
- **Type:** trial
- **Place:** Ghana
- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2014-11-26
- **Class:** treatment/ACT; diagnostic
- **Population:** febrile children presenting to outpatient clinic
- **Impact:** The test-treat package improved diagnosis and treatment of febrile children, reducing unnecessary anti-malarial and antibiotic prescriptions and inpatient admissions compared to routine outpatient care.
- **Effect:** proportion clinically well on day 7 99.2% vs 80.7%

- **Follow-up:** 7 days

### Open-label, randomized, non-inferiority clinical trial of artesunate-amodiaquine versus artemether-lumefantrine fixed-dose combinations in children and adults with uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Côte d'Ivoire.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (25409546)

- **Status:** published

- **Class:** treatment/ACT

- **Impact:** AS-AQ was non-inferior to AL, with both regimens showing high PCR-adjusted cure rates (96.8% vs 99%) and 100% PCR-adjusted ACPR in per-protocol analysis.

### Host candidate gene polymorphisms and associated clearance of P. falciparum amodiaquine and fansidar resistance mutants in children less than 5 years in Cameroon.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (25388906)
- **Journal:** Pathogens and global health
- **Type:** trial
- **Place:** Cameroon
- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2014-11-12
- **Class:** treatment/ACT
- **Population:** children less than 5 years
- **N:** 760
- **Impact:** SNPs in IL22, IL-4R1, and CD36 were associated with clearance of amodiaquine- and sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine-resistant P. falciparum parasites in Cameroonian children.
- **Effect:** odds ratio CD36 OR=0.27; IL22 OR=1.44; IL-4R1 OR=1.31 (95% CI CD36: 0.13-0.54; IL22: 1.06-1.95; IL-4R1: 1.07-1.83)
- **Species:** P. falciparum
- **Link:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25388906/

### Malaria, schistosomiasis and soil transmitted helminth burden and their correlation with anemia in children attending primary schools in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (25372029)
- **Journal:** PloS one
- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Not applicable
- **Place:** Democratic Republic of Congo
- **Design:** cross-sectional baseline survey (from a randomized controlled trial)
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2014-11-05
- **Class:** chemoprevention
- **Population:** primary schoolchildren aged 4 to 13 years
- **N:** 616
- **Impact:** Malaria and S. mansoni infections were strongly associated with a high prevalence of anemia in Congolese schoolchildren.
- **Effect:** adjusted odds ratio (aOR) for anemia Plasmodium spp: aOR 4.1; S. mansoni: aOR 3.3 (95% CI Plasmodium spp: 2.6-6.5; S. mansoni: 1.4-7.8)
- **Species:** P. falciparum

### Characterization of an in vivo concentration-effect relationship for piperaquine in malaria chemoprevention.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (25355697)
- **Journal:** Science translational medicine
- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Phase 3
- **Place:** Thailand
- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2014-10-29
- **Class:** chemoprevention; treatment/ACT
- **Population:** healthy adult male subjects
- **N:** 1000
- **Impact:** Piperaquine plasma concentrations of 6.7 ng/ml and 20 ng/ml reduced the hazard of malaria infection by 50% and 95% respectively, and simulations suggested a revised monthly dosing regimen could reduce malaria incidence by 70% in small children compared to current manufacturer recommendations.
- **Effect:** IC50/IC95 plasma concentration for hazard reduction; simulated incidence reduction IC50=6.7 ng/ml, IC95=20 ng/ml; 70% reduction in incidence with revised dosing
- **Follow-up:** 9 months
- **Link:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25355697/

### Preserving ACTs - Text Reminders to Increase Adherence to ACT Treatment
- **Source / ID:** clinicaltrials (NCT01722734)
- **Journal:** PloS one
- **Type:** registration
- **Phase:** Not applicable
- **Place:** Ghana
- **Design:** RANDOMIZED, PARALLEL, NA

- **Intervention(s):** Text message reminders

### Impact of a spatial repellent on malaria incidence in two villages in Sumba, Indonesia.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (25311699)
- **Journal:** The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Not applicable
- **Place:** Indonesia (Sumba)
- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2014-10-13
- **Class:** spatial repellent
- **Population:** adult men living in malaria-endemic households (sentinels of new infection)
- **N:** 180
- **Impact:** Spatial repellent coils reduced malaria infections by 52% and indoor mosquito landing rates by 32% compared to placebo, but the difference was not statistically significant after adjusting for intra-cluster correlation.
- **Effect:** protective effect (percent reduction in malaria infections) 52%
- **Follow-up:** 6 months
- **Link:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25311699/

### Combining organophosphate-treated wall linings and long-lasting insecticidal nets fails to provide additional control over long-lasting insecticidal nets alone against multiple insecticide-resistant Anopheles gambiae in Côte d'Ivoire: an experimental hut trial.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (25301219)
- **Journal:** Malaria journal
- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Not applicable
- **Place:** Côte d'Ivoire
- **Design:** experimental hut trial
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2014-10-09
- **Class:** ITN/LLIN
- **Population:** wild free-flying Anopheles gambiae mosquitoes in experimental huts
- **Impact:** Combining pirimiphos-methyl-treated wall lining or net wall hangings with LLINs did not significantly improve mosquito control or personal protection over LLINs alone, and did not manage insecticide resistance.
- **Effect:** mortality rate LLIN plus p-methyl WL 73% vs LLIN alone 63% (not significant improvement)
- **Species:** P. falciparum
- **Link:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25301219/

### Antirelapse Efficacy of Various Primaquine Regimens for Plasmodium vivax.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (25295216)
- **Journal:** Malaria research and treatment
- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Phase 3
- **Design:** open label, randomized, controlled, parallel group, assessor blind, phase 3
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2014-09-10
- **Class:** treatment/ACT
- **Population:** P. vivax malaria patients
- **Impact:** Recurrence and relapse rates were higher in the no-primaquine group compared to the three primaquine regimens, confirming primaquine's antirelapse activity, but low concordance between methods and probable resistance warrant caution.
- **Effect:** recurrence rate 16.39% (A) vs 8.07% (B), 10.07% (C), 6.62% (D)
- **Species:** P. vivax
- **Link:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25295216/

### Efficacy of artemisinin-based combination treatments of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in under-five-year-old Nigerian children.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (25246693)
- **Journal:** The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Phase 3
- **Place:** Nigeria
- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2014-09-22
- **Class:** treatment/ACT
- **Population:** children under 5 years with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
- **N:** 747
- **Impact:** Both artemether-lumefantrine and artesunate-amodiaquine were highly efficacious, safe, and well tolerated for treating uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Nigerian children under five, with artesunate-amodiaquine showing faster fever and parasite clearance.
- **Effect:** PCR-corrected cure rate 96.9% (AL), 98.3% (AA) (95% CI 93.9-98.2% (AL); 96.1-99.3% (AA))
- **Species:** P. falciparum
- **Follow-up:** 28 days
- **Link:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25246693/

### A randomized trial of artesunate-amodiaquine versus artemether-lumefantrine in Ghanaian paediatric sickle cell and non-sickle cell disease patients with acute uncomplicated malaria.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (25236838)
- **Journal:** Malaria journal
- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Phase 3
- **Place:** Ghana
- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2014-09-19
- **Class:** treatment/ACT
- **Population:** children with sickle cell disease and non-sickle cell disease (HbAA genotype) with acute uncomplicated malaria
- **N:** 119
- **Impact:** Parasite clearance was slower in sickle cell disease children compared with non-sickle cell disease children, but artesunate-amodiaquine and artemether-lumefantrine showed similar clinical and parasitological efficacy in both groups.
- **Effect:** Adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) rate on day 28 98.3% (SCD) vs 100% (non-SCD)
- **Species:** P. falciparum
- **Follow-up:** 42 days
- **Link:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25236838/

### A cluster-randomized controlled trial to assess the effectiveness of using 15% DEET topical repellent with long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs) compared to a placebo lotion on malaria transmission.

### Randomized comparison of the efficacies and tolerabilities of three artemisinin-based combination treatments for children with acute Plasmodium falciparum malaria in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (25001306)
- **Journal:** Antimicrobial agents and chemotherapy
- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Not applicable
- **Place:** Democratic Republic of the Congo
- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2014-07-07
- **Trial period:** 2011 to 2012
- **Class:** treatment/ACT
- **Population:** children with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
- **N:** 684
- **Impact:** All three artemisinin-based combination treatments were well tolerated and rapidly effective, with PCR-corrected cure rates similar across arms (92.7-94.3%), though dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine provided a longer post-treatment prophylactic effect and higher PCR-uncorrected cure rate.
- **Effect:** PCR-corrected cure rate 93.4% (amodiaquine-artesunate), 92.7% (artemether-lumefantrine), 94.3% (dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine)
- **Species:** P. falciparum
- **Follow-up:** 42 days
- **Link:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25001306/

### A phase III trial to evaluate the efficacy, fabric integrity and community acceptance of Netprotect using a recommended long-lasting insecticidal net as positive control.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (24998677)
- **Journal:** Malaria journal
- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Phase 3
- **Place:** Cambodia
- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2014-07-07
- **Class:** ITN/LLIN
- **Population:** households using long-lasting insecticidal nets in rural Cambodia
- **Impact:** Netprotect failed to meet WHO/WHOPES bio-efficacy criteria at 12, 24 and 36 months and showed faster insecticide degradation than the reference LLIN PermaNet 2.0, which met the criteria throughout the study.
- **Effect:** proportion meeting WHO bio-efficacy criteria 71% of Netprotect nets met criteria after 3 years (vs required 80%)
- **Follow-up:** 36 months
- **Link:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24998677/

- **Follow-up:** 1 year
- **Link:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24215565/

### The effect of antenatal monthly sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine, alone or with azithromycin, on foetal and neonatal growth faltering in Malawi: a randomised controlled trial.

### Persistence of Plasmodium falciparum parasites in infected pregnant Mozambican women after delivery.

- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2010-11-01

- **Population:** pregnant women

- **Species:** P. falciparum
- **Follow-up:** 28 days
- **Link:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18267042/

### [Comparative impact of three malaria preventive regimens during pregnancy on maternal anemia due to malaria in Burkina Faso].

- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Not applicable

- **Effect:** treatment effect (standard deviations) and grade difference 0.2 SD (no post-trial prophylaxis), 0.4 SD (<1 y post-trial prophylaxis); 0.52 grades higher educational attainment (95% CI -0.03 to 0.5 SD; 0.1 to 0.8 SD; -0.041 to 1.089 grades)
- **Species:** P. falciparum
- **Follow-up:** approximately 14-16 years (traced in 2001)
- **Link:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17013430/

### Geographic differences in antimalarial drug efficacy in Uganda are explained by differences in endemicity and not by known molecular markers of drug resistance.

### Evidence basis for antimalarial policy change in Sierra Leone: five in vivo efficacy studies of chloroquine, sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine and amodiaquine.

- **Species:** P. falciparum
- **Follow-up:** 6 months

### Randomized comparison of chloroquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine versus artesunate plus mefloquine versus artemether-lumefantrine in the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in the Lao People's Democratic Republic.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (15486837)

- **Type:** trial
- **Place:** Lao People's Democratic Republic (southern Laos)
- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published

- **Class:** treatment/ACT
- **Population:** patients with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
- **N:** 330
- **Impact:** Artesunate plus mefloquine and artemether-lumefantrine achieved high 42-day cure rates (100% and 97%) and faster parasite clearance than chloroquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (93% cure rate), which showed higher treatment failure.
- **Effect:** 42-day cure rate 100% (artesunate+mefloquine), 97% (artemether-lumefantrine), 93% (chloroquine+sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) (95% CI 2.0-2.1)

- **Follow-up:** 42 days

### Randomized trial of 3-dose regimens of tafenoquine (WR238605) versus low-dose primaquine for preventing Plasmodium vivax malaria relapse.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (15486831)

- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published

- **Class:** treatment/ACT

- **Impact:** Tafenoquine, including doses as low as a single 600-mg dose, was significantly more effective than low-dose primaquine at preventing P. vivax relapse after chloroquine treatment.

### Is amodiaquine failing in Rwanda? Efficacy of amodiaquine alone and combined with artesunate in children with uncomplicated malaria.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (15482401)
- **Journal:** Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH

- **Place:** Rwanda
- **Design:** randomized controlled trial

- **Class:** treatment/ACT
- **Population:** children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
- **N:** 308
- **Impact:** Combining amodiaquine with artesunate significantly reduced clinical and total treatment failure compared to amodiaquine alone, though rising amodiaquine resistance raises concerns for its use as first-line therapy in Rwanda.
- **Effect:** odds ratio (total treatment failure) 0.34 (95% CI 0.17-0.67)
- **Species:** P. falciparum
- **Follow-up:** 28 days

### Impact of a double dose of sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine to reduce prevalence of pregnancy malaria in southern Mozambique.

- **Impact:** Two doses of sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine significantly reduced the prevalence of peripheral and placental malaria parasitaemia and improved birthweight compared to placebo among adolescent pregnant women in Mozambique.

### Efficacy of monthly tafenoquine for prophylaxis of Plasmodium vivax and multidrug-resistant P. falciparum malaria.

- **Place:** Thailand

- **Status:** published

- **Impact:** Monthly tafenoquine was highly effective and safe for preventing P. vivax and multidrug-resistant P. falciparum malaria in Thai soldiers.
- **Effect:** protective efficacy 97% (all malaria); 96% (P. vivax); 100% (P. falciparum) (95% CI 82%-99% (all malaria); 76%-99% (P. vivax); 60%-100% (P. falciparum))

- **Follow-up:** 6 months

### Efficacy of chloroquine, sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine and amodiaquine for treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Kajo Keji county, Sudan.

- **Place:** Kajo Keji county, Sudan
- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2004-09-01
- **Class:** treatment/ACT

- **N:** 328
- **Impact:** Amodiaquine had the lowest failure rate (25.2%), while chloroquine (93.9%) and sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine (69.9%) showed very high failure rates, indicating none were suitable as monotherapy.

### Intermittent preventive sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine treatment of primigravidae reduces levels of plasma immunoglobulin G, which protects against pregnancy-associated Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (15321995)
- **Journal:** Infection and immunity
- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Phase III
- **Place:** Kenya
- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2004-09-01
- **Class:** IPTp
- **Population:** primigravidae (pregnant women, first pregnancy)
- **Impact:** Kenyan primigravidae receiving sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine IPTp had significantly lower levels of VSA(PAM)-specific IgG, which mediates protection against pregnancy-associated malaria, than women receiving placebo, with levels declining further with more IPTp doses.
- **Effect:** VSA(PAM)-specific IgG level lower in SP-IPTp group vs placebo, dose-dependent decrease

### Artesunate plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for uncomplicated malaria in Kenyan children: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (15307433)
- **Journal:** Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Phase 3
- **Place:** Kenya
- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2003-01-01
- **Trial period:** 1999 to 2000
- **Class:** treatment/ACT
- **Population:** children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
- **N:** 600
- **Impact:** Adding 3 days of artesunate to SP significantly reduced treatment failure rates compared with SP alone, while 1 day of artesunate reduced failure only by day 14, and overall SP resistance remained high enough to question the combination's suitability for widespread use in Kenya.
- **Effect:** risk difference in treatment failure rate (day 28) -20.0% (3-dose artesunate vs SP alone) (95% CI -29.4 to -10.6)

### Increases in correct administration of chloroquine in the home and referral of sick children to health facilities through a community-based intervention in Bougouni District, Mali.

- **Trial period:** 2001 to 2002
- **Class:** treatment/ACT

- **Impact:** The intervention significantly increased knowledge of danger signs, quality of counselling, correct home administration of chloroquine, and referral of sick children to community health centres compared to the comparison group.

### Artesunate with mefloquine at various intervals for non-severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (15306704)
- **Journal:** The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Phase 3
- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2004-08-01
- **Class:** treatment/ACT
- **Population:** patients with non-severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria
- **N:** 360
- **Impact:** Artesunate and mefloquine given simultaneously or at 8 or 24 hour intervals showed similar efficacy and pharmacokinetics with no drug interaction, but parasite recurrence occurred in 26-33% of patients, indicating single-dose combination therapy does not fully prevent recurrence or mefloquine resistance.
- **Effect:** parasite recurrence rate 26%, 26%, and 33% in groups A, B, and C respectively

### Efficacy of a 14-day primaquine regimen in preventing relapses in patients with Plasmodium vivax malaria in Mumbai, India.

- **Impact:** A 14-day supervised primaquine regimen reduced recurrences compared to no antirelapse therapy, but PCR-SSCP genotyping revealed a true relapse rate suggesting probable primaquine resistance in some cases.

### Low-dose quinine is effective in the treatment of chloroquine-resistant Plasmodium falciparum malaria in eastern Sudan.

- **Status:** published

- **Trial period:** 2002 to 2002
- **Class:** treatment/ACT
- **Population:** Patients with chloroquine-resistant Plasmodium falciparum malaria presenting at a health centre
- **N:** 93
- **Impact:** Once-daily low-dose quinine (15 mg/kg/day) was as effective as thrice-daily quinine (30 mg/kg/day) in treating chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum malaria, with no significant difference in parasite clearance or recrudescence rates among the three dosing regimens.

- **Journal:** Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Phase 3
- **Place:** Tanzania
- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2004-06-01
- **Class:** treatment/ACT
- **Population:** Children under five years with clinical, uncomplicated malaria
- **N:** 117
- **Impact:** SP produced better clinical recovery (98%) than CQ (90%), but pre-existing parasitological resistance (RII/RIII) was found in 14% of SP-treated and 51% of CQ-treated patients prior to SP's adoption as first-line treatment.
- **Effect:** proportion with RII/RIII parasitological resistance 14% (SP) vs 51% (CQ)
- **Species:** P. falciparum
- **Follow-up:** 28 days
- **Link:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15099990/

### Antimalarial efficacy of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, amodiaquine and a combination of chloroquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in Bundi Bugyo, western Uganda.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (15078262)
- **Journal:** Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Not applicable
- **Place:** Uganda
- **Design:** randomized, open-label, in vivo antimalarial efficacy study
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2004-04-01
- **Trial period:** 2002 to 2002
- **Class:** treatment/ACT
- **Population:** children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
- **N:** 268
- **Impact:** Chloroquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (Uganda's first-line regimen) and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine showed high PCR-adjusted failure rates, with amodiaquine performing best, suggesting the need to replace CQ+SP with a more efficacious regimen such as artesunate plus amodiaquine.
- **Effect:** PCR-adjusted treatment failure proportion at day 28 SP 37.0%, AQ 20.6%, CQ+SP 22.8% (95% CI SP 27.1-47.7; AQ 11.7-32.1; CQ+SP 14.1-33.6)
- **Species:** P. falciparum
- **Follow-up:** 28 days
- **Link:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15078262/

### A randomized trial of amodiaquine and artesunate alone and in combination for the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in children from Burkina Faso.

- **Journal:** Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH

- **Place:** Burkina Faso

- **Status:** published

- **Class:** treatment/ACT

- **Impact:** Artesunate alone and artesunate plus amodiaquine combination therapy resulted in faster parasite and fever clearance than amodiaquine alone, with all treatments highly efficacious and well tolerated.
- **Effect:** parasite clearance time (days) AR 1.13 days, AQAR 1.13 days vs AQ 1.6 days

### Activities of artesunate and primaquine against asexual- and sexual-stage parasites in falciparum malaria.

- **Class:** treatment/ACT

- **N:** 176
- **Impact:** Artesunate reduced the appearance of gametocytemia and shortened parasite clearance times compared to quinine, while primaquine accelerated gametocyte clearance without affecting therapeutic response.
- **Effect:** relative risk of gametocytemia appearance 0.34 (95% CI 0.17 to 0.70)
- **Species:** mixed

- **Impact:** AQ/SP combination was significantly more efficacious than CQ/SP or SP alone, with lower parasitological failure rates at day 28.

- **Impact:** Both mefloquine monotherapy and mefloquine-artesunate combination therapy were fully effective with no recurrences of parasitaemia at 28 days, though the combination therapy cleared parasites faster and reduced gametocyte carriage more than monotherapy.

### Optimising operational use of artesunate-mefloquine: a randomised comparison of four treatment regimens.

- **Status:** published

- **Impact:** The 3-day directly observed artesunate-mefloquine regimen resulted in no recrudescence and fewer P. vivax infections and less post-treatment anaemia compared with single-dose regimens, making it the most effective treatment despite single-dose observed regimens also being highly effective.

### Compliance with 14-day primaquine therapy for radical cure of vivax malaria--a randomized placebo-controlled trial comparing unsupervised with supervised treatment.

- **Place:** Pakistan
- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published

- **Trial period:** 2000 to 2001
- **Class:** treatment/ACT

- **Impact:** Both supervised and unsupervised 14-day primaquine treatment were equally effective at reducing P. vivax relapse compared to placebo, showing that unsupervised treatment with simple instructions can achieve compliance similar to supervised treatment.

### Reduction of malaria during pregnancy by permethrin-treated bed nets in an area of intense perennial malaria transmission in western Kenya.

- **Class:** ITN/LLIN

- **Impact:** In gravidae 1-4, permethrin-treated bed nets reduced malaria parasitemia, severe anemia, placental/maternal malaria, and low birth weight during pregnancy, with no benefit observed in gravidae five or higher.

- **Status:** published

- **Impact:** All 4 placebo volunteers developed parasitaemia and malaria symptoms, while none of the 12 atovaquone-proguanil recipients acquired malaria, demonstrating causal prophylactic (liver-stage) efficacy allowing discontinuation 7 days after exposure.

### Randomized comparison of mefloquine-artesunate versus quinine in the treatment of multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria in pregnancy.

- **Follow-up:** 2 years (May 1996 endpoint)

### Single dose artemisinin-mefloquine treatment for acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria.

### Susceptibility of Plasmodium falciparum to different doses of quinine in vivo and to quinine and quinidine in vitro in relation to chloroquine in Liberia.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (1934240)
- **Journal:** Bulletin of the World Health Organization
- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Not applicable
- **Place:** Liberia
- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 1991-01-01
- **Class:** treatment/ACT
- **Population:** Children infected with Plasmodium falciparum
- **N:** 64
- **Impact:** Quinine and quinidine remained effective against P. falciparum isolates in vitro despite chloroquine resistance, though chloroquine-resistant isolates showed roughly twice the IC50/IC90/MIC for quinine compared to chloroquine-sensitive isolates; in vivo, a single day (3-dose) quinine regimen resulted in recrudescence in 5 of 15 children, whereas longer regimens (2, 4, 7 days) prevented recrudescence, with recurrences only due to reinfection.
- **Effect:** Difference in IC50/IC90/MIC for quinine between chloroquine-resistant and chloroquine-sensitive isolates approximately 2-fold higher in resistant isolates
- **Species:** P. falciparum
- **Follow-up:** 28 days
- **Link:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/1934240/

### Indoor Residual Spraying With Fludora Fusion for Malaria Control in Pyrethroid-Resistant Areas of Gujarat, India: A Community-Randomized Trial.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (39949897)
- **Journal:** Journal of tropical medicine
- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Not applicable
- **Place:** India (Gujarat: Kheda, Vadodara, Panchmahal districts)

- **Trial period:** 2017 to 2018
- **Class:** ITN/LLIN; IRS
- **Population:** villages/houses in pyrethroid-resistant malaria vector areas

- **Impact:** Fludora Fusion showed longer residual efficacy (6 months) than bendiocarb (3-4 months) and reduced indoor resting density, parous rate, and entomological inoculation rate of Anopheles culicifacies compared to bendiocarb-sprayed houses.

### The Impact of Antenatal Azithromycin and Monthly Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine on Maternal Malaria during Pregnancy and Fetal Growth: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

- **N:** 1320
- **Impact:** Monthly SP and monthly SP plus azithromycin both reduced malaria parasitemia during pregnancy compared to two-dose SP, but neither intervention affected fetal biparietal diameter or femur length growth velocity, and azithromycin added no significant additional benefit over monthly SP alone.

### Artemether-lumefantrine efficacy among adults on antiretroviral therapy in Malawi.

- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Not applicable
- **Place:** Malawi
- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published

- **Population:** Adults (≥18 years) living with HIV on antiretroviral therapy (ART) for ≥6 months with undetectable viral load and CD4 ≥250/mm3, who developed uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria

- **Species:** P. falciparum
- **Follow-up:** 6 months postdischarge
- **Link:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36313146/

### The Duration of Protection from Azithromycin Against Malaria, Acute Respiratory, Gastrointestinal, and Skin Infections When Given Alongside Seasonal Malaria Chemoprevention: Secondary Analyses of Data from a Clinical Trial in Houndé, Burkina Faso, and Bougouni, Mali.

- **Impact:** Both qPCR and db-PCR-NALFIA detected substantial residual submicroscopic parasitemia at day 7 after microscopically successful treatment with pyronaridine-artesunate or artemether-lumefantrine, with no significant difference between the two treatments, and db-PCR-NALFIA positivity was associated with treatment failure while qPCR positivity was not.

- **Species:** P. falciparum
- **Follow-up:** 7 days
- **Link:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30105967/

### Treatment of adults with acute uncomplicated malaria with azithromycin and chloroquine in India, Colombia, and Suriname.

- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2017-10-13
- **Class:** treatment/ACT
- **Population:** adults with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
- **Impact:** Azithromycin 1 g plus chloroquine QD for 3 days was inferior to established comparator agents (SPCQ in India, AP in Colombia/Suriname), but increasing azithromycin dose to 2 g improved response rates to 97%.
- **Effect:** parasite clearance rate difference India: 84% (AZCQ) vs 94% (SPCQ); Colombia/Suriname: 57% (AZCQ) vs 99% (AP) (95% CI India: -22.6 to 0.8; Colombia/Suriname: -52 to -32)

- **Impact:** Monthly artesunate-amodiaquine given as seasonal malaria chemoprevention to school-aged children reduced clinical malaria cases substantially compared to no intervention, with only 3 cases in the ASAQ arm versus 20 in the control arm.

- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2017-12-28
- **Class:** treatment/ACT

### Factors contributing to anaemia after uncomplicated falciparum malaria in under five year-old Nigerian children ten years following adoption of artemisinin-based combination therapies as first-line antimalarials.

- **Impact:** Ten years after ACT adoption, anaemia remains common before and shortly after treatment in Nigerian children, with drug-attributable falls in haematocrit >4% being common and significantly lower in anaemic compared to non-anaemic children.

- **Impact:** Cure rates for both Artemether-Lumefantrine and Artesunate-Amodiaquine were higher during the dry season than the rainy season, largely due to a higher incidence of new infections (reinfections) during the rainy season.

### Malaria illness mediated by anaemia lessens cognitive development in younger Ugandan children.
- **Source / ID:** pubmed (27076184)
- **Journal:** Malaria journal
- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Not applicable
- **Place:** Uganda
- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published

- **Class:** chemoprevention; treatment/ACT
- **Population:** infants enrolled at 4-6 months, followed to 2 and 3 years of age; HIV-exposed uninfected and HIV-unexposed uninfected children

- **Impact:** Malarial illness episodes negatively predicted cognitive performance at 2 and 3 years, an effect mediated by anaemia, and this relationship was stronger in HIV-exposed uninfected children, while dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine was highly protective against malaria and anaemia but trial arm itself was not associated with neurodevelopmental outcomes.

- **Effect:** absolute risk reduction in Pf positivity MMP: 90% reduction (ARR 9%); FSAT: 66% reduction (ARR 4.9%)
- **Species:** mixed
- **Follow-up:** 6 months
- **Link:** https://doi.org/10.1101/2024.11.26.24318027

### Safety and efficacy of the blood-stage malaria vaccine RH5.1/Matrix-M in Burkina Faso: interim results of a double-blind, randomised, controlled phase 2b trial in children
- **Source / ID:** europepmc (PPR925537)
- **Journal:** medRxiv
- **Type:** preprint
- **Phase:** Phase 2b
- **Place:** Burkina Faso
- **Design:** double-blind, randomised, controlled, phase 2b
- **Status:** preprint
- **Published:** 2024-10-16
- **Trial period:** 2023
- **Class:** vaccine
- **Population:** children aged 5-17 months
- **N:** 361
- **Impact:** RH5.1/Matrix-M vaccine was safe, well tolerated, and showed vaccine efficacy of 55% with a delayed third dose regimen and 40% with a monthly regimen against clinical malaria compared to pooled controls.
- **Effect:** vaccine efficacy 55% (delayed third dose); 40% (monthly regimen) (95% CI 20-75% (delayed); -3-65% (monthly))
- **Species:** P. falciparum
- **Follow-up:** 6 months post-third vaccination
- **Link:** https://doi.org/10.1101/2024.10.15.24315473

### Artemether-lumefantrine-amodiaquine or artesunate-amodiaquine combined with single low-dose primaquine to reduce<i>Plasmodium falciparum</i>malaria transmission in Ouélessébougou, Mali: a five-arm, phase 2, single-blind, randomised clinical trial
- **Source / ID:** europepmc (PPR953171)
- **Journal:** medRxiv
- **Type:** preprint
- **Phase:** Phase 2
- **Place:** Ouélessébougou, Mali
- **Design:** five-arm, single-blind, phase 2, randomised clinical trial, per protocol analysis
- **Status:** preprint
- **Published:** 2024-02-24
- **Trial period:** October 2022 to December 2022
- **Class:** treatment/ACT
- **Population:** asymptomatic P. falciparum microscopy-detected gametocyte carriers aged 10-50 years
- **N:** 100
- **Impact:** Artemether-lumefantrine, with or without amodiaquine, and artesunate-amodiaquine plus primaquine nearly eliminated mosquito infectivity within 48 hours, whereas artesunate-amodiaquine alone left substantial residual transmission.
- **Effect:** median percentage reduction in mosquito infection rate 100% (artemether-lumefantrine, artemether-lumefantrine-amodiaquine, artemether-lumefantrine-amodiaquine+primaquine, artesunate-amodiaquine+primaquine) vs 31.67% (artesunate-amodiaquine alone) (95% CI IQR 100-100 (primaquine/artemether-lumefantrine arms); IQR -10.9-100 (artesunate-amodiaquine arm))
- **Species:** P. falciparum
- **Follow-up:** 2 days (48 hours) post-treatment
- **Link:** https://doi.org/10.1101/2024.02.23.24303266

### Artemisinin-naphthoquine plus lower-dose primaquine to treat and prevent recurrence of Plasmodium vivax malaria: an open-label randomized and non-inferiority trial
- **Source / ID:** europepmc (PPR693635)
- **Journal:** Research Square
- **Type:** preprint
- **Place:** China-Myanmar border
- **Design:** open-label, randomized, non-inferiority trial
- **Status:** preprint
- **Published:** 2023-07-18
- **Class:** treatment/ACT
- **Population:** patients with P. vivax malaria infection
- **N:** 288
- **Impact:** The artemisinin-naphthoquine plus lower-dose primaquine over 3 days (ANPQ3) regimen was not non-inferior to chloroquine plus primaquine over 14 days (CQPQ14) in preventing recurrence, but cleared fever and parasites faster, had fewer severe adverse effects, and had better medication adherence.
- **Effect:** difference in recurrence-free patients (percentage points) by day 182 3.5 (95% CI -8.6 to 1.5)
- **Species:** P. vivax
- **Follow-up:** 365 days
- **Link:** https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-3165342/v1

### Artemether-lumefantrine with or without single-dose primaquine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus amodiaquine with or without single-dose tafenoquine to reduce<i>Plasmodium falciparum</i>transmission: a phase 2 single-blind randomised clinical trial in Ouelessebougou, Mali
- **Source / ID:** europepmc (PPR811905)

- **Type:** preprint
- **Phase:** Phase 2
- **Place:** Ouelessebougou, Mali

- **Trial period:** 2021 to 2021
- **Class:** SMC; treatment/ACT
- **Population:** asymptomatic individuals aged 10-50 years with P. falciparum gametocytaemia
- **N:** 80
- **Impact:** Artemether-lumefantrine alone nearly completely prevented mosquito infections, whereas sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus amodiaquine left considerable post-treatment transmission that was reduced by adding tafenoquine.
- **Effect:** median percentage reduction in mosquito infection rate 100% (AL), 100% (AL+primaquine), 63.60% (SP+AQ), 100% (SP+AQ+tafenoquine) (95% CI AL: 97.2-100; AL+PQ: 100-100; SP+AQ: 0.62-100; SP+AQ+TQ: 100-100)
- **Species:** P. falciparum
- **Follow-up:** 7 days
- **Link:** https://doi.org/10.1101/2024.02.27.24303370

- **Source / ID:** europepmc (PPR785264)

### Will a lack of fabric durability be their downfall? Impact of textile durability on the efficacy of three types of dual-active-ingredient long-lasting insecticidal nets: A secondary analysis on malaria prevalence and incidence from a cluster-randomized trial in north-west Tanzania
- **Source / ID:** europepmc (PPR809518)

- **Type:** preprint
- **Phase:** Not applicable
- **Place:** Tanzania
- **Design:** cluster-randomized trial, secondary analysis
- **Status:** preprint
- **Published:** 2024-02-22
- **Trial period:** 2019 to 2022
- **Class:** ITN/LLIN
- **Population:** community residents and a cohort of children
- **Impact:** Torn nets showed reduced protection against malaria, but Chlorfenapyr-PY and PBO-PY LLINs maintained superior protection compared to pyrethroid-only nets even when torn.
- **Effect:** incidence rate ratio 0.76 (good condition vs extremely torn); 0.37 (too-torn PBO-PY vs intact PY); 0.45 (too-torn Chlorfenapyr-PY vs intact PY); 0.49 (intact Chlorfenapyr-PY vs intact PY, year 2) (95% CI 0.63-0.92; 0.19-0.72; 0.33-0.97; 0.29-0.81)

- **Link:** https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-3974056/v1

- **Follow-up:** 3 years (prevalence), 2 years (incidence cohort)

- **Trial period:** 2017 to 2019
- **Class:** ITN/LLIN
- **Population:** children aged 2-10 years in surveyed households
- **N:** 104
- **Impact:** PBO LLINs reduced malaria parasite prevalence and Anopheles mosquito density more than conventional pyrethroid-only LLINs 25 months after distribution.
- **Effect:** prevalence ratio (adjusted for baseline) 0.80 (95% CI 0.69-0.93)
- **Species:** P. falciparum
- **Follow-up:** 25 months
- **Link:** https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.4081085

### Entomological Effects of Attractive Targeted Sugar Bait Station Deployment in Western Zambia: Vector Surveillance Findings from a Two-arm Cluster Randomized Phase III Trial
- **Source / ID:** europepmc (PPR861309)
- **Journal:** Research Square
- **Type:** preprint
- **Phase:** Phase 3
- **Place:** Zambia
- **Design:** two-arm cluster-randomized controlled trial, phase 3
- **Status:** preprint
- **Published:** 2024-06-03
- **Trial period:** 2021
- **Population:** Anopheles funestus mosquito populations in study clusters (entomological surveillance)
- **N:** 20
- **Impact:** ATSB deployment was associated with a non-significant 35% reduction in vector light trap density, with no significant effects on parity, HLC rates, sporozoite prevalence, or EIR.
- **Effect:** rate ratio (light trap abundance) RR = 0.65 (95% CI 95% CI 0.30-1.40)
- **Species:** P. falciparum
- **Follow-up:** two 7-month deployments
- **Link:** https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-4450785/v1

### A Cluster Randomized Trial of Delivery of Intermittent Preventive Treatment of Malaria in Pregnancy at the Community Level in Malawi
- **Source / ID:** europepmc (PPR408798)
- **Journal:** Research Square
- **Type:** preprint
- **Phase:** Not applicable
- **Place:** Malawi
- **Design:** cluster randomized controlled trial, difference in differences analysis
- **Status:** preprint
- **Published:** 2021-10-18
- **Trial period:** 2018-11 to 2020-07
- **Class:** IPTp
- **Population:** pregnant women; women who delivered in the prior 12 months
- **N:** 1057
- **Impact:** Community health worker delivery of IPTp did not significantly increase IPTp3+ coverage compared to health facility delivery, though ANC4+ coverage increased significantly more in the intervention group.
- **Effect:** difference-in-differences in IPTp3+ coverage 6.9% (95% CI -5.9%, 19.6%)
- **Follow-up:** 21 months (baseline December 2017 to endline August 2020)

### Effectiveness and safety of reactive focal mass drug administration (rfMDA) using dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine to reduce malaria transmission in very low-endemic setting of Eswatini: a pragmatic cluster randomised controlled trial
- **Source / ID:** europepmc (PPR296389)
- **Journal:** medRxiv
- **Type:** preprint
- **Phase:** Not applicable
- **Place:** Eswatini
- **Design:** pragmatic, cluster-randomised controlled trial, intention-to-treat
- **Status:** preprint
- **Published:** 2021-03-12
- **Trial period:** 2015 to 2017
- **Class:** MDA; treatment/ACT; diagnostic
- **Population:** individuals residing near confirmed malaria index cases in a very low-endemic setting
- **N:** 77 clusters
- **Impact:** rfMDA using dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine was safe and resulted in lower cumulative malaria incidence than RACD, but the trial could not confirm its effectiveness, likely due to insufficient statistical power.
- **Effect:** adjusted incidence rate ratio (aIRR) 0.93 for all malaria; 0.77 for locally acquired malaria (95% CI 0.54-1.60 (all malaria); 0.38-1.56 (locally acquired malaria))
- **Species:** P. falciparum
- **Follow-up:** Sept 2015–Aug 2017 (approximately 2 years)
- **Link:** https://doi.org/10.1101/2021.03.12.21252721

### Improving malaria preventive practices and pregnancy outcomes through a health education intervention: a randomized controlled trial
- **Source / ID:** europepmc (PPR267254)
- **Journal:** Research Square
- **Type:** preprint
- **Phase:** Not applicable
- **Place:** Nigeria
- **Design:** randomized controlled parallel-group trial
- **Status:** preprint
- **Published:** 2021-01-18
- **Class:** IPTp; ITN/LLIN
- **Population:** pregnant women attending antenatal care
- **N:** 372
- **Impact:** The health education intervention based on the IMB model significantly improved reported ITN use, reported IPTp uptake, and haematocrit levels, but had no significant effect on reported malaria diagnosis or birth weight.
- **Follow-up:** 4 months post-intervention and at end of pregnancy

### Monitoring of Fabric Integrity and Attrition Rate of Dual-Active Ingredient Long-Lasting Insecticidal Nets in Tanzania: A Prospective Cohort Study Nested in a Cluster Randomized Controlled Trial
- **Source / ID:** europepmc (PPR758857)
- **Journal:** Preprints.org
- **Type:** preprint
- **Phase:** Not applicable
- **Place:** Tanzania
- **Design:** prospective cohort study nested in a cluster randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** preprint
- **Published:** 2023-11-13
- **Trial period:** 2019
- **Class:** ITN/LLIN
- **Population:** households in villages receiving distributed LLINs
- **N:** 3072
- **Impact:** All dual active ingredient LLINs had poor textile durability with median functional survival less than three years, with OlysetTM Plus performing worst and having the shortest survival.
- **Effect:** median functional survival (years) 1.9 years (Interceptor®, Interceptor® G2, Royal Guard®); 0.9 years (OlysetTM Plus)

### Effect of biannual azithromycin distribution on antibody responses to malaria, bacterial, and protozoan pathogens among children: A cluster-randomized, placebo-controlled trial in Niger
- **Source / ID:** europepmc (PPR316443)
- **Journal:** medRxiv
- **Type:** preprint
- **Phase:** Not applicable
- **Place:** Niger
- **Design:** cluster-randomized, placebo-controlled, double-masked, repeated cross-sectional secondary analysis
- **Status:** preprint
- **Published:** 2021-04-26
- **Class:** monoclonal antibody
- **Population:** children ages 1-59 months
- **N:** 3814
- **Impact:** Biannual azithromycin distribution was associated with lower Campylobacter spp. seroprevalence and seroconversion rate compared to placebo, with no significant differences for other pathogens including P. falciparum.
- **Effect:** seroconversion hazard ratio (Campylobacter spp.) 0.71 (95% CI 0.56-0.89)

### Efficacy and safety of artesunate-amodiaquine and artemether-lumefantrine and prevalence of molecular markers associated with resistance, Guinea: an open-label two-arm randomised controlled trial
- **Source / ID:** europepmc (PPR175912)
- **Journal:** Research Square
- **Type:** preprint
- **Phase:** Phase 3
- **Place:** Guinea
- **Design:** open-label, two-arm, randomised controlled trial, phase 3
- **Status:** preprint
- **Published:** 2020-06-15
- **Trial period:** 2016 to 2016
- **Class:** treatment/ACT
- **Population:** children aged 6-59 months with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
- **N:** 421
- **Impact:** Both artesunate-amodiaquine and artemether-lumefantrine showed high (99-100%) corrected efficacy at Day 28 with no evidence of artemisinin resistance-associated pfk13 mutations.
- **Effect:** Kaplan-Meier corrected efficacy at Day 28 100% (Maferinyah, both arms); 99% (Labé, both arms) (95% CI 97.2-100% (ASAQ, Labé); 97.1-100% (AL, Labé))

- **Follow-up:** 28 days

### Cost-effectiveness of Insecticide-treated wall liner and indoor residual spraying as additions to insecticide-treated bed nets to prevent malaria: findings from cluster randomized trials in Tanzania
- **Source / ID:** europepmc (PPR304335)
- **Journal:** Research Square
- **Type:** preprint
- **Phase:** Not applicable
- **Place:** Tanzania
- **Design:** cluster-randomized, two-arm, controlled trial (44 clusters); cost-effectiveness analysis
- **Status:** preprint
- **Published:** 2021-03-29
- **Trial period:** 2015 to 2016
- **Class:** ITN/LLIN; IRS
- **Population:** households in malaria-endemic areas of Muheza and Muleba, Tanzania
- **N:** 5666
- **Impact:** The ITWL trial was stopped early because the wall liner lost its insecticidal effect within 90 days, while IRS was found to be effective (57% efficacy) but more cost-effective than ITWL at averting malaria-related DALYs.
- **Effect:** efficacy (IRS) / incremental cost-effectiveness ratio 57% efficacy; ICER $490 per DALY averted (95% CI 3%-81% (efficacy); 61-1651 DALYs averted (95% CI))
- **Species:** P. falciparum
- **Follow-up:** 90 days (ITWL trial before termination)
- **Link:** https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-257460/v1

### A Cluster Randomized Trial of Delivery of Intermittent Preventive Treatment of Malaria in Pregnancy at the Community Level in Burkina Faso
- **Source / ID:** europepmc (PPR196773)
- **Journal:** Research Square
- **Type:** preprint
- **Phase:** Not applicable

- **Status:** preprint
- **Published:** 2020-08-05
- **Trial period:** 2017 to 2018
- **Class:** IPTp
- **Population:** pregnant women
- **N:** 734
- **Impact:** Community delivery of IPTp by CHWs led to a higher median number of IPTp doses received and higher IPTp3/IPTp4 coverage compared to standard facility-based delivery, though differences were not statistically significant for IPTp3/IPTp4 or ANC attendance.
- **Effect:** difference in differences (DiD) in coverage IPTp3: 17.6%; IPTp4: 20.0%; ANC4: 12.6% (95% CI IPTp3: 95% CI -16.3 to 51.5; IPTp4: 95% CI -7.2 to 47.3)

### Comparing drug regimens for clearance of malaria parasites in asymptomatic adults using PCR in Kilifi County, Kenya: an open-label randomised controlled clinical trial (MalPaC)
- **Source / ID:** europepmc (PPR113925)
- **Journal:** Wellcome Open Res
- **Type:** preprint
- **Phase:** Not applicable
- **Place:** Kilifi County, Kenya
- **Design:** open-label, randomised controlled trial
- **Status:** preprint
- **Published:** 2020-02-20
- **Trial period:** 2013-11 to 2014-02
- **Class:** vaccine; treatment/ACT
- **Population:** asymptomatic adults
- **N:** 90
- **Impact:** Falciparum DNA remained detectable by PCR post-treatment with incomplete parasite clearance regardless of drug regimen, though the AP+AS regimen may have partially suppressed acquisition of new infections and reduced recrudescence compared to AS and SP+AS+PQ.
- **Effect:** Odds ratio for qPCR positivity in post-treatment phase (AS and SP+AS+PQ vs AP+AS) OR=7.7 (AS vs AP+AS); OR=4.2 (SP+AS+PQ vs AP+AS) (95% CI 4.6-12.8 (AS); 2.6-6.8 (SP+AS+PQ))
- **Species:** P. falciparum

### Community case management to accelerate access to healthcare in Mali: a realist process evaluation nested within a cluster randomized trial.
- **Source / ID:** europepmc (39058651)
- **Journal:** Health policy and planning
- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Not applicable
- **Place:** Mali
- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2024-09-01
- **Population:** children under 5 and pregnant women; also CHWs, health providers and community participants
- **N:** 195
- **Impact:** Both arms saw doubled treatment-seeking and antenatal visits and halved under-5 mortality over 3 years compared with baseline, but proactive CHW home visits had only modest effects on care utilization and no effect on under-5 mortality compared with control.

### Efficacy of a spatial repellent for control of malaria in Indonesia: a cluster-randomized controlled trial
- **Source / ID:** europepmc (PPR88800)
- **Journal:** medRxiv
- **Type:** preprint
- **Phase:** Not applicable
- **Place:** Indonesia
- **Design:** cluster-randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
- **Status:** preprint
- **Published:** 2019-08-13
- **Trial period:** 2015 to 2018
- **Class:** spatial repellent
- **Population:** children aged 6 months to 5 years, after radical cure
- **N:** 1341
- **Impact:** The spatial repellent (transfluthrin) reduced malaria infection compared to placebo, but the overall effect across 24 clusters was not statistically significant, though subgroup analyses in higher-risk clusters showed significant protective effects.
- **Effect:** protective efficacy 27.7% (first infection) and 31.3% (overall infections) across 24 clusters; 33.3% and 40.9% in 19 clusters with baseline infection; 60% in 12 moderate-to-high-risk clusters
- **Species:** P. falciparum
- **Follow-up:** 24 months
- **Link:** https://doi.org/10.1101/19003426

### Effect of biological larviciding with Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis for malaria control on non-target vector mosquito species in rural Burkina Faso – A cluster randomized trial

- **Type:** preprint

- **Design:** cluster-randomized trial

- **Published:** 2019-10-15
- **Class:** ITN/LLIN; larval source management

### Field performance of three mosquito collection methods for assessing the entomological efficacy of dual-active ingredient long-lasting insecticidal nets.
- **Source / ID:** europepmc (37507478)

- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Not applicable
- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2023-07-28
- **Class:** ITN/LLIN
- **Population:** Anopheles mosquitoes collected in households in trial clusters
- **N:** 60
- **Impact:** All three mosquito collection methods (HLC, CDC light traps, PSC) detected fewer mosquitoes in the Interceptor G2 dual-active-ingredient LLIN arm compared to other trial arms, with HLC and PSC showing stronger evidence of this effect due to more frequent collection rounds.

### Distance to Health Centers and Effectiveness of Azithromycin Mass Administration for Children in Niger: A Secondary Analysis of the MORDOR Cluster Randomized Trial.
- **Source / ID:** europepmc (38100110)
- **Journal:** JAMA network open
- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Not applicable
- **Place:** Niger
- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2023-12-01
- **Trial period:** 2014 to 2017
- **Population:** children aged 1 to 59 months
- **N:** 76092
- **Impact:** Mass azithromycin administration reduced child mortality more among children living farther from primary health centers, with mortality reduction ranging from 0% at 0 km to 28% at 10 km distance.
- **Effect:** mortality reduction (%) with azithromycin vs placebo by distance to health center 0% at 0 km, 4% at 1 km, 16% at 5 km, 28% at 10 km (95% CI -19% to 17% (0 km); -12% to 17% (1 km); 7% to 23% (5 km); 17% to 38% (10 km))
- **Follow-up:** 2 years
- **Link:** https://doi.org/10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2023.46840

- **Type:** preprint

- **Design:** cluster-randomized, stepped-wedge trial
- **Status:** preprint
- **Published:** 2020-09-04
- **Trial period:** 2016-11 to 2017-04
- **Population:** children under-5 presenting with acute illness at village clinics
- **N:** 6965
- **Impact:** Children in the eCCM intervention phase were more likely to be urgently referred to higher-level health facilities than those in the control phase, with no significant increase in re-consultation or hospitalization rates after adjusting for time.

### Impact of universal home visits on child health in Bauchi State, Nigeria: a stepped wedge cluster randomised controlled trial.

- **Impact:** Universal home visits to pregnant women and their spouses reduced childhood diarrhoea prevalence and improved diarrhoea management, hygiene knowledge and practices, with only a slight, non-significant improvement in full immunisation.

### Antibiotic Review Kit for Hospitals (ARK-Hospital): a stepped wedge cluster randomised controlled trial

- **Class:** diagnostic

### Macrolide and Nonmacrolide Resistance with Mass Azithromycin Distribution.
- **Source / ID:** europepmc (33176084)
- **Journal:** The New England journal of medicine
- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Not applicable
- **Place:** Niger
- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2020-11-01
- **Population:** preschool children 1 to 59 months of age in villages receiving mass drug administration
- **N:** 30
- **Impact:** Villages receiving twice-yearly mass azithromycin distribution for 4 years had substantially higher levels of macrolide and nonmacrolide (including beta-lactam) antibiotic resistance determinants than villages receiving placebo.
- **Effect:** ratio of macrolide-resistance determinants (azithromycin vs placebo) 7.5 times as high at 48 months (7.4 times as high at 36 months) (95% CI 3.8 to 23.1 (48 months); 4.0 to 16.7 (36 months))
- **Follow-up:** 48 months
- **Link:** https://doi.org/10.1056/nejmoa2002606

### The global network antenatal corticosteroids trial: impact on stillbirth.
- **Source / ID:** europepmc (27255082)
- **Journal:** Reproductive health
- **Type:** trial
- **Phase:** Not applicable
- **Place:** India, Pakistan, Zambia, Kenya, Guatemala, Argentina
- **Design:** randomized controlled trial
- **Status:** published
- **Published:** 2016-06-02
- **Class:** treatment/ACT
- **Population:** pregnant women at risk of preterm birth and their newborns
- **N:** 102
- **Impact:** The antenatal corticosteroids intervention was associated with a non-significant increased risk of stillbirth overall, with a significant increase among term births and macerated stillbirths.
